Subject (in full) Release of Convict Yien Tsoong (閻中) on the
30th November 1934.

Made by D.S. Poole Forwarded by JBRm s/

Convict Yien Tsoong who was arrested on Haiphong
Road near Ferry Road at about 6 p.m. April 2nd, 1932 on a
charge of propagating communism and who was due for release
on the 26th November 1934, was removed from the Shanghai
Special District Court and handed over to the Shanghai
Public Safety Bureau on the 30th November 1934 to be sent
to the House of Reflection in Soochow.

Particulars regarding the release of this convict
have been recorded for future reference.

Subject (in full) Arrest of Yien Tsoong ( 中 ) for being in possession of a quantity of blank forms of enrollment to the Communist Party.

Made by D.I.Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by D.Bhu. D.I.

According to our records No.522 Connaught Road,
the address given by the above mentioned accused, is the same
place where Liao Zung Yih (廖識一) used to live. This
individual, it will be recalled, was arrested together with
two others by the Municipal Police on March 21, 1932, during
the course of a raid on the head uarters of the "Anti-Japanese
and National Salvation Federation of Workers of Various Trades"
at No.19 Macao Road where a large quantity of communist
literature was unearthed (Vide I.R. 23.3.32) A search of
his lodgings at 522 Connaught Road resulted in the discovery
of a quantity of pro-communist books. Whether Yien Tsoong
is acquainted with Liao Zung Yih is not known, but the
information regarding the latter has been communicated to
Gordon Road Station.

Attached herewith are two specimens of the
enrolment forms together with translations.

Kuh Pao-hwa

The following is the statement of Yien Tsoong( 宗 ),
native of Kaifeng, taken by me C.D.S.90 Tsang Kyung Loong,

at G. R. Stn. on the 2/4/32, and interpreted by Kao Chien.

Yien Tsoong, age 25, native of Kaifeng, Honan, S/Student, re-
siding at 522 Sun Sun Lee, Connaught Road.
In July 19th Year of Chinese Republic, I came to Shanghai from
Kaifeng, and studied in China University, Woosung. At the
begining of February, 1932, I came to Shanghai and stayed with
my friend named Liang Tien Ngoo( 梁天牛 ) in the Modern
Middle School, 47 Markham Road, and at the same time asked him
to get some job for me. At the middle of March, 1932, this
school removed to Ave. Haig, where a 'Union of Students Suffering
from War District' was then organized. I took abode there.
On the 31/3/32, I heard that this school was going to stop, so
I removed out and stayed with my friend named Tsang Ts Chung
